title: The Sweet Porridge (Sweet Soup)

full_text:
Once upon a time, there lived a poor, pious little girl and her widowed mother at the edge of a village. They were so impoverished that they had not even a crust of stale bread left in the cupboard. Weeping with hunger, the girl walked into the forest, where an ancient, kindly woman took pity on her.

The old woman gave her a small iron cooking pot and instructed: "Whenever you say, 'Cook, little pot, cook,' it will boil sweet, rich porridge. When you say, 'Stop, little pot, stop,' it will cease cooking."

The girl brought the pot home, and she and her mother enjoyed sweet, delicious porridge every day, banishing their hunger forever.

One morning, while the girl was out walking, the mother felt hungry and said, "Cook, little pot, cook!" The pot began bubbling with fragrant, sweet porridge. The mother ate until she was satisfied, but when she wished the pot to cease, she forgot the magic words! She said, "No more, little pot!" and "That is enough!" but the pot kept boiling.

Porridge poured over the rim, filled the kitchen, covered the parlor, surged out into the street, and flowed into neighboring cottages as if it meant to feed the entire universe! The terrified villagers climbed upon their roofs as sweet porridge flooded the lane.

At last, the little girl returned home. Seeing the sweet river, she called out clearly, "Stop, little pot, stop!" The pot instantly ceased boiling. But whoever wished to enter the village for the next three days was obliged to eat his way through a street of sweet porridge!
moral: Blessings bring abundant nourishment, but carelessness with instructions leads to overflowing chaos.
